findings.finding: SignedDigitUniqueness.eval reads least-significant-first Int coefficients. ReverseAdd.pairs is the literal zipWith addition of a digit list and its reverse. Canonical normalization preserves eval b digits + reversedValue b digits.

ResetNormalization.ordinaryTags replaces all Bool reset flags with false. PhysicalWidth.actualDigits applies ordinaryTags before atActualWidth; its final carry and every emitted digit use the original continuous carry recurrence, independently of stored flags. A reset-placed list is not the actual digit list.

PhysicalWidth.placed retains a terminal slot. actualDigits omits that slot exactly when its computed terminal carry is zero. Bounded nonnegative coefficients with b>=2 force carry bits and hence width L or L+1. When terminal=1 the actual output is body ++ [1], so its reflection is L-i, not L-1-i.

ActualBaseBirths.incoming b xs k is terminal b 0 of the ordinary-tagged prefix xs.take k. The quotient carry_bit theorem uses b>=2, coefficient bounds 0..2*b-2, and an incoming bit. No arbitrary guessed carry is substituted for this prefix recursion.

PhysicalWidth.PositiveLast requires an actual last digit greater than zero and excludes the empty list. ReverseAdd.reverse_add_normalization derives bounded actual digits, positive last digit, exact width and numeric reverse-add value from b>=2, bounded input digits, PositiveLast input and literal coefficient projection xs.map fst = pairs digits. It derives the required bounded coefficients from the same projection.

findings.topic: Base two versus inherited rigidity claims
findings.finding: SignedDigitUniqueness and BaseReflection rigidity and SeamSafety defect/palindrome statements retain explicit b>=3 hypotheses. Binary counterexamples are present in the original sources. The b>=2 carry, residue, actual digit length/bounds and reverse-add normalization lemmas used by the new birth theorem do not depend on these b>=3 conclusions.

BaseBirths.localPair uses one shared source coefficient and two carry bits. ActualBaseBirths identifies this pair with actual output only under terminal=0. These definitions do not by themselves justify overflowing output; the new adjacent classifier and shifted-index bridge are a required distinct composition.

Every original module was copied by exact pinned bytes into a new compact source directory and rebuilt with the official 4.19.0 compiler and --trust=0. Both public-root print-axiom checks and exhaustive module-origin theorem dependency checks passed. Four compiler-produced unsafe List.mapTR implementation constants were recorded separately; no project theorem depends on them, and no safe custom axiom was admitted.

The original APIs concern finite coefficient/digit words. They supply no run-population, ancestry, lifetime, infinite-avoidance or 196 conclusion. The new interior birth theorem must retain its index bounds, coefficient symmetry and terminal-one hypothesis; endpoint identities and canonical specialization have separately stated domains.
